items.summary: The Iran SNSC determination closes Thursday evening without formal announcement — Day 14 of contested compliance, with the Doha indirect talks now the primary resolution signal. Iran Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi announced that working groups have been formed to follow up on implementation of the June 17 MOU, confirming that consultations are continuing to determine time and place for formal negotiations through Qatar and Pakistan as mediators. This is the first confirmed Iranian diplomatic movement since Iran's commitment to meet Qatari mediators July 1 — the Doha engagement represents a positive directional shift in the Hormuz formal resolution pathway even as the SNSC has not issued a formal compliance determination. Physical Hormuz traffic continues to build through the CENTCOM corridor, with oil prices declining toward pre-war levels on market confidence in the physical reopening. WTI is estimated in the approximately $63-67 range Thursday evening — Day 12 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor and approaching the pre-war equilibrium level — representing the market's strongest reopening-confidence signal yet. The decline is driven by physical traffic building (supply-positive) and the Doha engagement signal; Lebanon risk premium from Hezbollah's Day 5 non-compliance provides a partial upward offset. Approximately 80 mines remain in the central channel, constraining transit to CENTCOM-escorted routes. Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% of vessel value. The Lloyd's normalization gate remains formally closed — a formal SNSC position change is the upstream requirement for the 118-tanker backlog's full commercial release. The 60-day oil sanctions waiver (Day 15, through approximately August 18) provides approximately 46 days of structural time buffer. The Doha talks create an important analytic distinction: Iran is diplomatically engaged on MOU implementation follow-up without the SNSC having issued a formal compliance determination, which suggests the SNSC silence may reflect internal deliberation rather than resistance — a meaningful shift from the first two weeks of the compliance period. Iran's Foreign Minister's prior characterization of Swiss technical framework negotiations as producing 'no tangible progress' on uranium enrichment levels is now running parallel to the Doha implementation track, creating a two-track diplomatic architecture: implementation follow-up (Doha) and final-status nuclear access (Swiss). Lebanon advances to Hour ~244+ through Thursday evening. Hezbollah's 'null and void' rejection of the Rubio framework — issued June 28 by Naim Qassem — is now Day 5 operative. Five consecutive days of Hezbollah political non-compliance without military resumption is the ceasefire period's most durable post-rejection signal; the pattern continues to support the analytic read that the characterization is political positioning rather than operational prelude. IDF drone activity in southern Lebanon's 570 km² buffer zone continues Thursday. No formal void declaration has been issued. The SNSC's continued silence creates a structural complexity: Hezbollah's political rejection removes the Lebanese withdrawal pathway that would give the SNSC domestic justification for a formal re-closure retraction, while the Doha talks suggest Iranian willingness to engage on implementation regardless.

items.summary: The International Energy Agency Thursday issued a statement characterizing Ukraine's drone and missile strike campaign against Russian oil refining infrastructure as 'unprecedented in the history of the Russia-Ukraine conflict' — a formal multilateral energy body assessment that elevates the Ukrainian economic warfare strategy from a tactical success to a validated strategic milestone. More than 20% of Russia's total national refining capacity has been knocked offline by a campaign of more than two dozen strikes since March, including eight of Russia's ten largest refineries. The scale of disruption has produced domestic fuel shortages across 55 of Russia's 83 federal entities — more than two-thirds of the country — with mandatory government-imposed restrictions on gasoline and diesel sales or private company-imposed restrictions operative simultaneously. Putin publicly acknowledged the shortages, an extraordinary admission given Russian state media's typical embargo on reporting domestic infrastructure damage from the conflict. Russia is now in negotiations to import gasoline from Kazakhstan and potentially India — a reversal of the country's historical status as a net hydrocarbon exporter and a significant economic and symbolic concession. The Kapotnya refinery, the largest fuel supplier to the Moscow metropolitan region, was struck twice this month and will remain offline until at least the end of 2026 — the longest confirmed repair timeline of any struck facility. Crimea has escalated its emergency fuel restrictions to reserve gasoline and diesel for military and state use only, reflecting the peninsula's compounded exposure to both the broader domestic distribution failure and its geographic isolation from mainland distribution chains. The IEA designation has direct strategic implications: Ukrainian targeting of Russian oil infrastructure has forced Russia toward import dependency for domestic fuel supply — a dynamic with direct military logistics implications for front-line fuel chains in Zaporizhzhia and Kupyansk corridors that draw from the same disrupted distribution network. Ukraine executed two additional refinery strikes June 28, extending the campaign's momentum into the current brief period. Russia's ballistic missile production (74/month) and guided glide bomb projection (75,000+ in 2026) continue as the parallel offensive posture backdrop. Peru ONPE: Day 28 of the count. Keiko Fujimori has been declared the winner by election authorities, with the JNE (National Electoral Jury) scheduled to issue a formal presidential declaration by July 3 — tomorrow. Fujimori, with approximately 50,000 more votes than Roberto Sánchez per the JNE count of all ballots, will become Peru's first elected female president. Sánchez has not conceded and raised fraud claims; however, international election monitors confirmed finding no evidence of fraud after polls closed. North Korea: Choe Hyon destroyer advances to Day 9 without new provocations. PRC 46-company ban Day 5; Taiwan coastguard patrol Day 33.

items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the June 2026 Employment Situation at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday — the week's primary market catalyst and the first of the two primary data inputs ahead of the July 29 FOMC rate decision. The consensus expectation entered July 2 at approximately +113,000 nonfarm payrolls, down from May's +172,000 print. The consensus decline reflects tariff cost absorption, the OBBB legislative uncertainty that characterized most of May and June, and the structural tech-sector headcount contraction backdrop. The three-month average through May stood at approximately 188,000 — substantially above the approximately 100,000 breakeven level — and will recalculate with the June print. May's 172,000 included approximately 70,000 from leisure and hospitality (partially FIFA World Cup hiring-related), suggesting June's hotel and event hospitality component may normalize downward as the PNW FIFA venues approach their July 7 conclusion. The June report's implications for the FOMC's October 2026 rate decision are direct: Chair Warsh's nine-hike-dot hawkish posture, with the October 2026 hike market-priced and PCE running at 4.1% (May), has set a high bar for a miss to repruce material downward FOMC probability. A June print at or above consensus sustains the October hike expectation; a significant miss below 80,000 would begin to compress the hike probability. The June CPI release July 14 constitutes the second primary input before the July 29 decision — both data points are now in-window. WTI crude oil is estimated in the approximately $63-67 range Thursday — Day 12 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor — as the Doha indirect talks engagement and continued physical Hormuz traffic building push the market toward pricing the reopening as structurally real. The monthly WTI decline of approximately 19% reflects the compound effect of the physical transit build, Doha diplomatic signal, and the 60-day sanctions waiver's extension of the structural time buffer. The $65-70 equilibrium range established over the prior two sessions is breaking toward pre-war floor levels ($60-65 range) as market confidence in the Doha track grows. This has direct downstream implications: the pump-relief chain (SNSC → Lloyd's → backlog release → supply pulse → pump price decline) may be partially advancing through the supply side even without formal Lloyd's gate opening, as market pricing changes affect domestic retail fuel pass-through. Oregon pump prices are estimated in the approximately $5.00-5.15/gallon range; national approximately $4.35-4.45/gallon, declining modestly. The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment remains near historic lows at approximately 48.9. US GDP Q1 2026 was confirmed at 2.1% annualized. FOMC rate at 3.50-3.75%. US 10-year Treasury yield approximately 4.38%.

items.summary: SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 entry on July 6 (Sunday) is four days out Thursday evening — the structural equity market event of the current brief cycle. The forced passive rebalancing is now characterized as follows: only 4.3% of SpaceX shares are free-floating, but Nasdaq's three-times multiplier applied under the May 1, 2026 revised methodology raises SpaceX's effective index weight to approximately $267 billion — approximately 0.6% of the Nasdaq-100. Passive funds tracking the index, including the $490 billion Invesco QQQ Trust, must buy SpaceX while selling displaced index members to maintain tracking. Estimated passive buying on the July 6 effective date ranges from $8-12 billion, with potential to surpass $600 billion if public float increases substantially over time. Pre-event positioning in SpaceX and adjacent tech names is intensifying Thursday-Friday as fund managers front-run the Sunday effective date. The forced selling in displaced Nasdaq-100 members creates parallel downward pressure on existing constituents that were purchased or overweighted in anticipation of the SpaceX entry. TD Securities has flagged the July 6 entry date as a key investor watch event, noting 'even bigger days ahead' as float restrictions may ease. The OBBB continues through Day 2 of implementation: Medicaid work requirements, SALT modification, top individual rate reduction (retroactive January 1, 2026), border security appropriations, and energy production incentives all operative. The state implementation readiness gap remains the primary near-term OBBB risk surface with CMS guidance on enforcement grace periods or waiver application frameworks not yet issued. Section 232 tariff enforcement (steel, aluminum, copper at 50%) advances to Day 31 — five full weeks operative. USTR de minimis proposed rules comment period closes July 6 — this Sunday, the same day as SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 entry — with the public hearing scheduled July 7. FERC large-load show-cause orders advance to Day 16; AI data center pathway explanation deadline at T-14 (approximately July 18) — final two weeks.

items.summary: The Tucannon Fire in southeastern Washington enters Day 5 of the East Cascades onset period with an estimated acreage of approximately 25,000-30,000+ acres — growth continuing from the 25,000+ acres reported at July 1 evening, driven by the second PNW heat wave now in Day 2 of its active intensification phase, which is extending and deepening the record-setting 100-hour fuel dryness environment that has characterized the onset period throughout. Level 3 (Go Now) evacuation orders remain active in Garfield County's Pomeroy area corridor. The second PNW heat wave — arriving less than 10 days after the season's first heat wave — is now producing its maximum fuel dryness amplification effect, with AccuWeather projecting record-challenging temperatures in Seattle and Portland through the holiday weekend. NOAA's July outlook confirming above-normal temperatures and drought conditions throughout the month frames the second heat wave not as an isolated event but as the onset of a sustained severe fire weather period. The July 4 holiday weekend is two days out — the compound convergence of active heat wave, record Tucannon fuel dryness, and maximum human ignition risk (fireworks, recreational activity, agricultural burning) creates the most elevated compound ignition-risk period of the onset season. The Hamilton Fire (near Winthrop, Okanogan County) has reached approximately 85% containment, with all Level 3 Go Now and Level 2 Get Set evacuation orders downgraded to Level 1 Get Ready advisories — a significant positive progression from Wednesday's full-town Winthrop evacuation. The fire's rapid partial stabilization from the acute emergency phase allows partial release of suppression resources toward the Tucannon commitment. The Hamilton Fire ignited from approximately 300 acres in the late morning before rapid wind-driven growth, now stabilizing at 82-85 acres for active suppression purposes with the surrounding landscape held. At the national scale: three federal wildland firefighters were killed on June 27 in a burnover incident on the Knowles and Gore fires in western Colorado — a shelter deployment event with two survivors treated for burn injuries. The Cottonwood Fire in Beaver County, Utah, has grown to approximately 92,000 acres as of Thursday, making it the largest active wildfire burning anywhere in the United States. Colorado and Utah governors have declared emergencies.
